aspect: The first one of the year
description: You have not had a agbalumo since last year and the first one resets something. The rest of the season is spent chasing that first one.
energy_note: A taste you had forgotten you were waiting for.

description: People who grew up with agbalumos know the week it begins without checking. The anticipation starts before the fruit does, which is the part the research says is free.
energy_note: Looking forward to it is most of it.
notes: Kumar, Killingsworth & Gilovich: anticipation of experiences is pleasurable and unrelated to cost.

description: Almost nobody eats the first agbalumo of the season alone. It is given, split, or brought back for you by someone who was passing the market.
No document, no permit, no border, no electricity, no institution. A few coins at most, and often not even that.
energy_note: Nothing on earth has to approve this.

aspect: It becomes a marker for the year
description: Decades later the smell of a agbalumo puts you in one specific childhood kitchen. It is doing memory work you never asked it to do.
energy_note: A fruit that files your whole childhood.
